candidates.exact_span: Unless otherwise indicated in this permit, if the EPA Region 6 MQL for a pollutant or pollutant parameter is sufficiently sensitive (as defined above) and the analytical test result is less than the MQL, then a value of zero (0) may be used for reporting purposes on DMRs. Furthermore, if the EPA Region 6 MQL for a pollutant or parameter is not sufficiently sensitive, but the analytical test result is less than the published ML from a sufficiently sensitive method, then a value of zero (0) may be used for reporting purposes on DMRs.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Different readings of when zero may be reported for sub-MQL/sub-ML results change which numeric value is compared against discharge limits (A) and how below-detection or no-result DMR entries are classified versus true numeric measurements (C).

candidates.exact_span: Discharges authorized in this individual permit are limited to once through cooling water, cooling tower blowdown, and storm water from the adjacent areas.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether a given facility discharge type falls within the authorized set determines which permit effluent limits apply (A), which monitoring obligations attach to that discharge point or flow (B), and whether a period without measurements reflects unauthorized discharge, conditional non-discharge, or another no-data state (C).

candidates.exact_span: There shall be no discharge of domestic sewage into waters of the United States.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Interpretation of whether domestic sewage is present or discharged affects whether associated monitoring and limit comparisons are required at all (B) and whether missing domestic-sewage results should be treated as documented no-discharge, unauthorized discharge, or unresolved (C).

candidates.exact_span: Discharges of storm water runoff from outfalls other than Outfalls 001 shall be covered under the NPDES Multi-Sector Storm Water Permit.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether a stormwater outfall is governed by this permit or the Multi-Sector permit changes which numeric limits are enforceable here (A), which monitoring schedule applies (B), and how to classify absent results for outfalls outside Outfall 001 (C).

candidates.exact_span: Runoffs from active quarry areas are not authorized.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Treating quarry runoff as unauthorized versus conditionally allowed under other clauses changes whether Outfall 001 limits and related monitoring apply (A,B) and whether no-data periods represent prohibited discharge, documented no-discharge, or unresolved evidence (C).

candidates.locator: page 7 / part_i / C. BEST MANAGEMENT PRACTICE / 2
candidates.exact_span: Discharges are restricted to overflows from the retention pond due to catastrophic or chronic precipitation events.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether a discharge event qualifies as a permitted retention-pond overflow during catastrophic or chronic precipitation determines if monitoring was required for that period (B) and whether missing measurements reflect conditional non-requirement versus inadequate evidence (C).

candidates.locator: page 7 / part_i / C. BEST MANAGEMENT PRACTICE / 3
candidates.exact_span: Discharges of storm water runoff from access roads in undisturbed areas shall be covered under the NPDES Multi-Sector Storm Water Permit.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Classification of a runoff source as access-road stormwater in undisturbed areas shifts applicable limits and monitoring from this permit to the Multi-Sector permit, changing which requirements are evaluated (A,B).

candidates.locator: page 7 / part_i / C. BEST MANAGEMENT PRACTICE / 4
candidates.exact_span: If a discharge of storm runoff from a quarry (mining) area is necessary, the discharge must comply with effluent limitations established at Outfall 001.
candidates.computation_change_reason: When quarry-area discharge is deemed necessary, Outfall 001 effluent limitations become the enforceable numeric limits and associated monitoring obligations apply; different interpretations of necessity or scope change A/B computations.

candidates.exact_span: If the State re-evaluates and updates the total maximum daily loads (TMDL) or final effluent limitation necessary to protect water quality standards during the life of this permit, and the effluent limitations are more stringent than those listed in this permit, or controls a pollutant not listed in this permit, then the permit may be modified or revoked and reissued to conform with the approved Water Quality Management Plan (WQMP) final effluent limitations.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether and when a permit modification under this reopener occurred during Federal FY2025 changes which numeric discharge limits are enforceable for compliance comparison.

candidates.locator: page 7 / part_i / E. WHOLE EFFLUENT TOXICITY TESTING (7 DAY CHRONIC NOEC)
candidates.exact_span: It is unlawful and a violation of this permit for a permittee or his designated agent, to manipulate test samples in any manner, to delay sample shipment, or to terminate or to cause to terminate a toxicity test.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Evidence of sample manipulation, delayed shipment, or test termination affects whether whole-effluent toxicity monitoring was validly performed as required (B) and whether absent or incomplete WET results reflect documented non-performance versus unresolved missing evidence (C).

candidates.locator: page 7 / part_i / E. WHOLE EFFLUENT TOXICITY TESTING (7 DAY CHRONIC NOEC)
candidates.exact_span: Once initiated, all toxicity tests must be completed unless specific authority has been granted by EPA Region 6 or the State NPDES permitting authority.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether a WET test was properly initiated, completed, or exempted by authority changes the applicable monitoring obligation for that event (B) and how incomplete or missing WET evidence is classified (C).
